transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

Since the freezer is still cold but the fridge is warm (around 10°C), this usually points to a cooling distribution issue rather than a complete failure of the compressor. In most integrated fridge-freezers, cold air is produced in the freezer and blown into the fridge via a fan and vents. The two most likely causes are:
1. Blocked airflow: Ice or frost may have built up behind the back panel of the fridge, blocking the vent that lets cold air through. This can happen after a power cut if the defrost cycle didn't complete properly.
2. Fan failure: The fan inside the freezer might have stopped, so no cold air is being pushed into the fridge section. Please check for ice at the back of the fridge compartment and listen for the fan running when the compressor is on.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Thanks. I can hear it running a lot, so I think the compressor is going. I can't see any vent in the fridge part though. There's some frost on the back of the freezer but not loads. What should I check next?

The compressor running constantly is a good sign that it's still trying to cool; this pattern (freezer cold, fridge warm) usually means the cold air isn't reaching the fridge section. This is most often caused by ice blocking the airflow vent behind the freezer panel, which happens if the automatic defrost system has failed. To guide you safely and accurately, I need the model number. It's usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment (often near the salad drawer). If you can see it without moving the appliance, please read out the 'Model' or 'Prod No'. If you can't reach it because of the kitchen door, tell me that too.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Found the label inside the fridge, it says HMCB 7030 AA. Hotpoint. Is that what you needed?

Thanks for that model number. This often happens after a power cut if the defrost cycle didn't complete. Please do a full manual defrost: switch it off at the wall socket, move food into cool bags, leave both doors open until all ice has melted (this may take 24 hours), then dry it and switch it back on. Let me know if the fridge cools down normally after this.
Ok, I can do that but I'd have to empty everything out first. Is a full defrost definitely the next step? Nothing smells burnt and it's not tripping anything, if that helps.

Yes, a full manual defrost is the most important next step because it clears any ice blocking the cold air vent. Please switch the appliance off at the wall socket, move food into cool bags with ice packs, leave both doors open for 24 hours to let all ice melt (put towels down), then dry everything and switch it back on. Let me know if the fridge cools down normally after this.
